title: Sliding Log-Volume Retention Budget for Delta Gates
originality_status: pending orthogonal-RNN, dynamical-isometry, log-determinant and constrained-gating audit; no priority claim
formal_object: For unit k_t, diagonal D_t with entries in (0,1], beta_t in [0,1), and ordinary Delta transition A_t=(I-beta_t k_t k_t^T)D_t, define per-step irreversible log-volume expenditure c_t=-log det A_t=-log(1-beta_t)-sum_i log d_(t,i). For B>=0 and integer W>=1, constrain every trailing W-token expenditure to at most B, with absent pre-sequence costs initialized to zero or a resumed cost queue verified feasible, and study the minimum-singular-value survival of the actual ordered frozen-feature product.

operations.input: Chronological product of diagonal-times-rank-one Delta transitions
operations.condition: Order is preserved and future coefficients are frozen
operations.output: Exact tagged-state propagation and determinant product

operations.input: Ordinary symmetric erase and contractive diagonal decay
operations.output: Each A has spectral norm at most one; ordered products are contractions

operations.input: Singular values, determinant and current residual
operations.condition: Each factor has spectral norm at most one; nonnormality itself is allowed and finite precision remains separate
operations.output: Exact correction expenditure plus a conservative state-survival lower bound

operations.input: Proposed gate log-cost and an available sliding budget
operations.condition: Projection is radial in nonnegative log-cost coordinates
operations.output: Causal feasible gates with c_t no larger than the available budget

operations.input: Rolling budget dependency and CE gradients
operations.condition: Each forward step reads W-1 realized costs; reverse dependence can propagate through the full remaining sequence
operations.output: Autodiff gradients almost everywhere and framework-selected subgradients at kinks; detaching the accumulator is a biased surrogate

operations.input: Determinant-one nonnormal/anisotropic matrices and zero-budget case
operations.condition: Counterexamples preserve the claim being tested
operations.output: Determinant alone is insufficient without a norm cap; retention is not correctness

derivation_steps.statement: The matrix determinant lemma gives det A_t=(1-beta_t) product_i d_(t,i).
derivation_steps.justification: det(I-beta kk^T)=1-beta for unit k, and determinants multiply without commuting the factors.

derivation_steps.statement: With post-decay state Sbar_t=D_t S_(t-1) and residual e_t=v_t-Sbar_t^T k_t, the post-update residual is e_t^+=v_t-S_t^T k_t=(1-beta_t)e_t, so -log(||e_t^+||/||e_t||)=-log(1-beta_t) when e_t is nonzero.
derivation_steps.justification: Write S_t=Sbar_t+beta_t k_t e_t^T, left-multiply by k_t^T and use ||k_t||=1.

derivation_steps.statement: Thus erase correction and state-volume loss share the exact scalar -log(1-beta); diagonal decay spends additional volume without improving the post-decay current residual.
derivation_steps.justification: Subtract the determinant decomposition from the residual identity.

derivation_steps.statement: For P=A_b...A_(a+1), every singular value is at most one and sigma_min(P)>=|det P|=exp(-sum_j c_j).
derivation_steps.justification: sigma_min=|det P|/product of the other singular values, whose product is at most one.

derivation_steps.statement: Write proposed costs a_i=-log d_i, b=-log(1-beta), c=b+sum a_i. With available p_t=B-sum previous W-1 costs, choose alpha=min(1,p_t/c) and set d_i=dtilde_i^alpha, beta=1-(1-betatilde)^alpha.
derivation_steps.justification: The realized log-cost is alpha c and is nonnegative, so it fits the remaining token-bucket budget and equals the original gates when inactive.

derivation_steps.statement: Every interval of at most W realized updates has sum c<=B and hence sigma_min(P)>=exp(-B); length H gives the blockwise loose bound exp(-ceil(H/W)B).
derivation_steps.justification: Use the sliding construction and apply the ordered-product inequality to each interval/block.

derivation_steps.statement: For a separate general oblique/nonnormal extension define c_j=-log|det A_j|. If only ||A_j||<=rho_j, then sigma_min(P)>=exp(-sum_j c_j)/(product_j rho_j)^(d-1).
derivation_steps.justification: Bound the other d-1 singular values by the product spectral norm. Here c_j need not be a nonnegative budget because an oblique determinant may exceed one; this exposes why the ordinary Delta token budget does not directly certify QED/D03.

assumptions: The theorem is for ordinary symmetric Delta erase with unit keys, beta strictly below one and contractive positive diagonal decay.
Future coefficients are frozen and shared between compared trajectories; full state-dependent neural dynamics require a Jacobian analysis.
The lower bound protects arbitrary real-arithmetic state perturbations, not semantic facts or future query alignment.
B>=0, W is a positive integer, proposed dtilde_i are finite in (0,1], proposed betatilde is finite in [0,1), and initialization or resume state satisfies the rolling budget.
The rolling budget is causal and prefix-only but introduces a sequential dependency for which no associative training scan is proved.
Finite precision can erase components below numerical resolution even when the real-arithmetic lower bound is positive.
Exact one-step replacement beta=1 is excluded because it makes A singular and consumes infinite log-volume budget.
Ordinary CE must learn when to spend budget; the theorem supplies no importance oracle.
The gate projection is piecewise differentiable. Min, max, equality at the budget boundary and the zero-cost branch use framework-selected subgradients at kinks.
method_expression: Let the existing gate network propose finite dtilde_i in (0,1] and betatilde in [0,1). Convert to nonnegative costs atilde_i=-log dtilde_i, btilde=-log(1-betatilde), ctilde=btilde+sum atilde_i. Maintain the preceding W-1 realized scalar costs and p_t=max(0,B-sum c_j). Set alpha=1 for ctilde=0 and otherwise min(1,p_t/ctilde); apply d_i=dtilde_i^alpha and beta=1-(1-betatilde)^alpha in the ordinary Delta recurrence. Train with ordinary teacher-forced CE. Ordinary autodiff gradients apply almost everywhere and the framework selects subgradients at kinks; exact reverse dependence may propagate across the full later sequence through the recurrent budget state, while a detached budget state is a declared biased surrogate.
distinguishing_prediction: For every frozen W-step product of the admitted ordinary Delta transitions, minimum singular value is at least exp(-B) up to numerical error, while updates equal the original proposed gates whenever the budget is inactive. If multiplicative attenuation materially causes long-range failure, tagged old-state components should survive longer at the explicit cost of weaker immediate correction; no benefit is predicted when collision, query misalignment or representational alias dominates.
falsifier: Reject practical necessity if a fixed small erase/decay gate with the same realized total expenditure is equivalent; the bound holds but native long-range behavior does not improve; revision/adaptation loss dominates; the sequential budget removes the compute advantage; or primary work already applies the same sliding log-volume constraint to Delta. A mathematical falsifier is an admitted ordinary Delta product whose minimum singular value is below exp(-sum c).
closest_alternative: Original Delta/GDN/KDA gates and a fixed beta/decay cap are the strongest simple baselines. RWKV-7 has richer removal/insertion gates; PDN changes directions with historical curvature; D03 changes write direction with a future-query metric; QED changes erase content and may be nonnormal; DeltaProduct simply adds microstep costs. Orthogonal/unitary RNNs, dynamical isometry, log-determinant regularization and constrained recurrent gating are serious unclosed nearest-work risks.
decisive_comparison: Primary-source review must first determine whether an existing recurrent method already projects sliding gate log-cost under a minimum-singular-value guarantee. If not, later comparison must match realized cumulative gate expenditure against a fixed-cap Delta and measure the correction-retention trade-off with native tasks; this card does not define or authorize that experiment.
complexity_and_information_access: Recurrent inference stores W scalar costs (or an equivalent queue) with O(1) rolling bookkeeping, applies O(d) gate transformation per token and uses no d^2 metric. It uses only current prefix gates and ordinary next-token labels. Exact training may retain O(T) additional scalar activations or recompute them because reverse dependence can cross the full remaining sequence; no chunkwise/associative formulation is established, so training parallelism may be worse even though recurrent inference is cheap. No GPU/runtime feasibility is claimed.
measurement_status: Existing native recall scores may observe delayed behavior but do not prove the stated attenuation mechanism. No new benchmark or score is created; direct mechanism identification remains a measurement gap.
